name: LMFAO
notes: Party electro-house rap-pop, and the structural fact the entry states is that the chorus is not the vocal: "instrumental drop as the real chorus", with documented electro-house practice putting the emphasis on "the climax or drop". So the arrangement gives the hook 16 bars against a 16-bar verse and drops out hard before it, and the harmony is functionally irrelevant by the entry's own admission — "minor-mode two-chord vamps with a saw riff carrying the identity" — which is a two-chord family set at `vamp`-weighted harmonic rhythm and the second-most triad-heavy chord block in the 2009-2012 block. The kit is the entry's: "electro-house kick on all four, huge layered clap on 2&4, 16th hats, and long white-noise/riser builds", hence riser/impact perc lanes at low density and a wide clap offset. The bass is the documented electro-house "dirty bass" with "grinding and whirring sawtooth b-lines" locked to the kick. Vocals are "rapped/chanted party verses with a shouted gang chorus", a low dense melody with an answering counter. ⚠ The research marks the harmony `[LOW-CONF]` and calls the parameters electro-house convention; both marks are repeated here, and every number above is INFERRED. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "minor-mode two-chord vamps with a saw riff carrying the identity", and "loops are 4 bars", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so a `vamp`-dominant weighting rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The two-chord vamp now sits on `1_per_bar`, which is the only value that reaches every chord of the four-chord families here inside a 4-bar loop; `vamp` stays as the minority. Kept to the two values the model already authored, so nothing new is claimed about the rate. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 945/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** The 1-bar value came out of `melody.phraseBars`, which is now [2,4] weighted [4,3]. `generators::melody` writes a phrase's rhythm **once** and reuses it for every repeat, so a 1-bar phrase gives the whole clip one bar of rhythmic entropy — and the counter, whose onsets are read off the lead's, inherits that ceiling. Distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "a single detuned saw riff as the hook; loops are 4 bars. Vocals are rapped/chanted party verses with a shouted gang chorus, plus a sung guest feature; the chorus is often instrumental with a chant on top.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
